Manahath (son of Shobal)
MAN-a-hath
proper noun
Hebrew manachath, “rest” or “resting place,” the name of a son of Shobal the Horite; a place also bears the name.

📖 Biblical Definition

Manahath was a son of Shobal, of the line of Seir the Horite, named second among Shobal’s children: “And the children of Shobal were these; Alvan, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shepho, and Onam” (Gen 36:23). The chronicler kept the same name in his book of generations (1Ch 1:40). This entry concerns the man; for there is also a place called Manahath, reckoned among the dwellings of the children of Benjamin and of certain families of Judah (1Ch 8:6), so that the careful reader distinguishes the person of Seir from the town of the later record. Manahath belonged to the Horites of Mount Seir, the people whom the LORD planted in that land aforetime and afterward dispossessed, giving their inheritance to the children of Esau (Deu 2:22). The dictionary records him, a name that signifies rest, to witness that the LORD numbers the families of the earth even when their own histories are silent. Manahath’s name speaks of rest, yet his people found no abiding rest in Mount Seir, for they were destroyed from before the children of Esau and dwelt there no more. The reader is taught that there remaineth a rest for the people of God which no earthly mountain can give, a rest that is not in any land of this passing world but in the LORD Himself, who is the everlasting habitation of His people, the same yesterday, today, and for ever.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A son of Shobal the Horite; the name is borne also by a place of the later record.

expand to see more

MANAHATH, a son of Shobal, the Horite, of the line of Seir.

His name stands second among the children of Shobal.

The name is borne also by a place reckoned among the dwellings of Benjamin and Judah.

He belonged to the Horites whom the LORD afterward dispossessed.

His name, signifying rest, witnesses to the rest that is in the LORD alone.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 36:23 — "And the children of Shobal were these; Alvan, and Manahath, and Ebal, Shepho, and Onam."

Gen 36:20 — "These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,"

Deu 2:22 — "As he did to the children of Esau, which dwelt in Seir, when he destroyed the Horims from before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead even unto this day:"

Psa 16:6 — "The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; he witnesses to the rest that is found not in any earthly land but in the LORD alone.

expand to see more

Manahath is a name among the sons of Shobal, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine him. The dictionary records the man, and marks him from the place of the same name reckoned among the dwellings of Benjamin and Judah, that the reader may know which Manahath is meant.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the sovereign providence of God over the rise and fall of peoples, and the truth that true rest is found in Him alone. Manahath’s name speaks of rest, yet the Horites found no abiding rest in Mount Seir; there remaineth a rest for the people of God which no earthly mountain can give, in the everlasting habitation of the LORD.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “rest” or “resting place,” this entry marks a son of Shobal the Horite.

Usage

"As Manahath’s name spoke of rest his people never kept, so no earthly land can give abiding rest."

"The LORD who numbered the sons of Shobal is Himself the everlasting habitation of His people."

"Let the reader labour to enter into that rest which remaineth for the people of God in the LORD alone."
